rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Passive solar siting and orientation'?
rows.expected: Sun-path diagram and solar altitude/azimuth for date and place (implement Reda-Andreas SPA from the NREL report, not NREL's C code), long-axis orientation check, overhang depth from sun angles, shadow casting from terrain/trees/neighbours (Source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified))
rows.expected_source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified)
rows.answer: A site-design CAD needs a sun-path model driven by latitude, date and time to evaluate solar gain on building faces, plus a true-north orientation setting so the building can be rotated against north. It also needs shading from terrain and neighbouring massing so siting options can be compared against winter and summer sun.
rows.note: Sun path by date/place, orientation, terrain/neighbour shading match; omits overhang depth and SPA.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Magnetic bearings in old deeds'?
rows.expected: Declination for date and place to rotate magnetic calls to true or grid north (Source: NOAA NCEI geomagnetic calculator https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/geomag/calculators/magcalc.shtml (unverified))
rows.answer: A site-design CAD must read metes-and-bounds calls with quadrant bearings and distances from old deeds, then convert magnetic bearings to true north using the declination for the survey date. Magnetic declination drifts over decades, so the deed's date matters for a correct boundary.
rows.note: Declination by survey date rotating magnetic calls to true north matches key fact.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle Nested, circular and oversized references?

rows.answer: Nested references load to a depth of 16, and circular references are stopped by a cycle chain of canonical paths. Oversized loads hit caps of 4,000,000 objects, 1,000 files, 512 MiB per file and 1 GiB total per load.
rows.note: Depth 16, canonical-path cycle chain; caps verified in load.rs; omits overlays not nested.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Passive solar siting and orientation'?
rows.expected: Sun-path diagram and solar altitude/azimuth for date and place (implement Reda-Andreas SPA from the NREL report, not NREL's C code), long-axis orientation check, overhang depth from sun angles, shadow casting from terrain/trees/neighbours (Source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified))
rows.expected_source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified)
rows.answer: It needs true-north-aware orientation plus sun-path and shadow/solar-access analysis (solar azimuth and altitude for the site's latitude, date and time). That should be combined with terrain slope and aspect so building long axes and glazing can face the equator-side (south in the northern hemisphere).
rows.note: Sun path, altitude/azimuth, long-axis orientation, shadows covered; omits overhang depth and SPA. No source.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Magnetic bearings in old deeds'?

rows.answer: It needs bearing-and-distance (COGO) entry in quadrant-bearing notation, with a magnetic-declination correction for the deed's date because declination drifts over time. It also needs legacy units (chains, rods, links) and a traverse misclosure report to check that the old description closes.
rows.note: Gives declination correction by deed date for magnetic bearings. No source vs NOAA calculator.

It also needs shading/light-distribution analysis on the ground, access and turning-radius checks, and area takeoffs split between PV and crop zones.
rows.note: Elevated PV rows, machinery spacing, crop light shading all covered. No source vs NREL InSPIRE.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Passive solar siting and orientation'?
rows.expected: Sun-path diagram and solar altitude/azimuth for date and place (implement Reda-Andreas SPA from the NREL report, not NREL's C code), long-axis orientation check, overhang depth from sun angles, shadow casting from terrain/trees/neighbours (Source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified))
rows.expected_source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified)
rows.answer: It needs a georeferenced site (latitude/longitude and true north, not just grid north) so it can work out sun position and sun paths for any date and time. With that it can run shadow and solar-access studies, so building long axes and glazing can be oriented toward the equator.
rows.note: Covers sun path for date and place, shadows and long-axis orientation; misses overhang depth. energy.gov source matches.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Magnetic bearings in old deeds'?
rows.expected: Declination for date and place to rotate magnetic calls to true or grid north (Source: NOAA NCEI geomagnetic calculator https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/geomag/calculators/magcalc.shtml (unverified))
rows.answer: It needs quadrant bearing entry (e.g. N 45°30' E) plus conversion from historical magnetic bearings to true or grid bearings, using the declination for that place on the deed's date. It also needs to rotate a whole traverse to a new basis of bearings, so old calls can be retraced and checked for closure.
rows.note: Key fact matches: declination for date and place rotates magnetic calls to true/grid. NOAA calculator matches.

rows.answer: It needs parametric PV array layout with panel height, tilt or tracking, row spacing and ground-coverage ratio, all set against crop rows and equipment lanes. It also needs shading and irradiance analysis at crop level, so energy yield and crop light can be balanced.
rows.note: Covers elevated PV rows with crop strips, equipment spacing and crop-light shading. No source given.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle XATTACH / -XREF attach, overlay, reload, unload, detach, path, type?
rows.expected: Status full: All options implemented with JSON and command-line forms; attach failure changes nothing (Evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks/xref.rs specs(); tests/xref.rs reload_unload_path_and_detach)
rows.answer: Fully: XATTACH and -XREF implement attach, overlay, reload, unload, detach, path and type in both JSON and command-line forms, and a failed attach changes nothing. One limit is that the Unloaded state is not saved, so every xref reloads when the drawing is reopened.
rows.note: Full status, JSON and command-line forms, failed attach changes nothing; Unloaded-state caveat is in card.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle Nested, circular and oversized references?
rows.expected: Status full: Depth <= 16, cycle chain by canonical path, overlays not nested, file/byte/object caps (Evidence: load.rs fetch(); test circular_and_deeply_nested_references_are_bounded)
rows.answer: It bounds them: nesting stops at depth 16, cycles are caught by tracking the chain of canonical paths, overlays are not nested, and a load is capped at 4,000,000 objects, 1,000 files, 512 MiB per file and 1 GiB in total. A reference that hits a limit becomes an empty block with a status, and the host drawing still opens.
rows.note: Depth 16, canonical-path cycles, overlays not nested, caps; numeric caps verified in load.rs.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle Fields, hyperlinks, dbConnect/OLE, DesignCenter, Excel links?

rows.note: None status, no command specs; DATALINK 8 MiB detail is in the card.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle CSV exports (TABLEEXPORT, DATAEXTRACTION)?
rows.expected: Status full: One-way exports (Evidence: cmd/table/cells.rs; cmd/blocks/extract.rs)

rows.note: Full, one-way CSV exports; cites cells.rs as expected.

rows.answer: It needs a sun-path diagram with solar altitude and azimuth for a given date and place (the Reda-Andreas SPA implemented from the NREL report, not NREL's C code), a long-axis orientation check, overhang depth from sun angles, and shadows cast by terrain, trees and neighbouring buildings.
rows.note: Sun path, SPA from NREL report, orientation, overhang, shadows all match; pvlib source.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Magnetic bearings in old deeds'?

rows.note: Declination for date and place to rotate to true/grid north; same NOAA URL, unverified noted.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Passive solar siting and orientation'?
rows.expected: Sun-path diagram and solar altitude/azimuth for date and place (implement Reda-Andreas SPA from the NREL report, not NREL's C code), long-axis orientation check, overhang depth from sun angles, shadow casting from terrain/trees/neighbours (Source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified))
rows.expected_source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified)
rows.answer: It needs a true-north/solar reference (site latitude, longitude, declination-corrected north arrow), sun-path and shadow studies for chosen dates/times, and the ability to rotate and test building footprints against slope aspect from a terrain surface. Glazing orientation and overhang shading checks round it out.
rows.note: Covers sun path, shadows, orientation and overhangs. Gives no source; expected cites NREL SPA.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Magnetic bearings in old deeds'?
rows.expected: Declination for date and place to rotate magnetic calls to true or grid north (Source: NOAA NCEI geomagnetic calculator https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/geomag/calculators/magcalc.shtml (unverified))
rows.answer: It needs quadrant-bearing input (e.g. N45°30'E) with distances for metes-and-bounds entry, a per-date, per-location magnetic declination correction (historic declination models such as NOAA's) to rotate old magnetic bearings to true or grid north, and closure/map-check reporting to reconcile the deed against modern survey. Unit handling for chains, rods and poles is also common.
rows.note: Date/place declination rotating bearings to true/grid north matches. Source field is none, not NOAA calculator.

rows.instruction: What does a site-design CAD need to support the technique 'Agrivoltaics'?

rows.answer: It needs array layout tools for panel rows (pitch, tilt, tracker axis, clearance height) placed on a terrain surface, shade and irradiance analysis to verify light reaching crops between rows, and equipment-access checks for farm machinery turning and row width. Drainage and fencing/setback rules tie it to the rest of the site plan.
rows.note: Elevated rows, equipment spacing, crop shading match. No source given; expected cites NREL InSPIRE.

rows.instruction: Why does a land-development CAD need 'Parametric zoning rule set (setbacks by yard, impervious %, coverage, height, parking ratios, buffers, well/septic/stream setbacks) with live compliance report' (Site rules)?

It also turns the submittal compliance table into a generated report rather than hand-filled numbers.
rows.note: Manual error-prone checking is the right idea; misses must-priority differentiator, spreadsheets and resubmittals.

rows.expected: 2025/2025.1: corridor surface builds 3-4x faster, object-snap moves on large corridors claimed 20-80x faster, MMS cache written only on change; Dynamo gained 1,120 nodes; 2026 added a modeless 3D viewer, Project Explorer Object Sets from the command line, corridor transition control, surface/corridor transparency and InfoDrainage-based drainage analysis. (Source: https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/aec/2024/08/19/whats-new-in-civil-3d-2025-1/ ; https://www.symetri.co.uk/insights/blog/whats-new-in-autodesk-civil-3d-2025/ ; https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/aec/2025/12/11/whats-new-in-civil-3d-2026-2)
rows.answer: Autodesk states faster surface and corridor rebuilds, improved data shortcut and Project Explorer workflows, and better large-drawing performance in recent releases, and some users echo quicker open/save and regen. I am unsure of specific percentage gains.
rows.note: Faster corridor/surface builds right direction; misses 3-4x, 20-80x, Dynamo nodes, 2026 additions.

rows.instruction: What do users complain about regarding Crash volume is structural, not incidental in CAD products in general?
rows.expected: Severity high: Autodesk's own fixed-issue lists carry ~17 crash/hang fixes in Civil 3D 2027.1 alone, ~12 in 2027, ~15 in 2026.1 and ~11 in 2026.2; 2024.3 fixed two cases where alignment data was lost after save and reopen. Forum users report weekly to daily crashes in 2026. (Source: https://help.autodesk.com/view/CIV3D/2027/ENU/?guid=civil_3d_fixed_issues_2027_1; https://help.autodesk.com/view/CIV3D/2026/ENU/?guid=civil_3d_fixed_issues_2026_1; https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/civil-3d-forum/civil-3d-2026-crashing/td-p/14083638)
rows.answer: Users say crashes are a routine part of daily CAD use rather than rare events ('fatal error' dialogs, daily crash reports), so they rely on frequent saves, autosave and backup files. They blame aging code bases, plug-ins and graphics drivers rather than one-off bugs.
rows.note: Daily crashes match the forum reports; misses Autodesk fixed-issue crash counts per release, the key evidence.

rows.instruction: What do users complain about regarding Xref paths break on move, drive mapping, permissions, cloud cache or VPN in CAD products in general?
rows.expected: Severity high: Relative paths are unavailable across drives or servers and can fail because 'automatic save is too frequent'; unresolved-xref causes include mapped-vs-UNC, drive letters hijacked by USB devices, paths over 256 chars, stopped DNS services; after a server migration opening drawings can freeze, with the advice to unplug the network cable; the Reference Manager bulk-repaths with no undo. (Source: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2027/ENU/?guid=GUID-164C2548-91E6-476D-AFDF-6257340C2EE2; https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/XREF-in-AutoCAD-is-Unresolved.html; https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/When-trying-to-attach-a-drawing-as-external-reference-with-a-relative-path-the-message-appears-Relative-path-cannot-be-assigned.html)
rows.answer: Users complain that xrefs stored with absolute paths or mapped drive letters break when files move, drive mappings differ per machine, permissions block access, or cloud caches (OneDrive, Desktop Connector) and VPNs make paths stale or slow. Reference Manager and eTransmit are the usual workarounds.
rows.note: Mostly restates question; misses relative-path cross-drive limit, USB letter hijack, long paths, no-undo repath.

rows.instruction: What do users complain about regarding Cloud worksharing discards local work in CAD products in general?
rows.expected: Severity high: Desktop Connector sync failures leave files 'Modified' and invisible to co-workers; a 'Conflict' gives priority to the cloud copy and local changes go to the Recycle Bin; 'Free Up Space' before sync deletes unsynced work; file locking is unsupported on long paths; the shortcut-sync balloon can appear before upload finishes so clicking it loads stale data. (Source: https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Losing-data-when-working-with-DWG-files-in-Desktop-Connector.html; https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/File-shows-Conflict-State-in-Desktop-Connector.html; https://help.autodesk.com/view/CIV3D/2023/ENU/?guid=Civil3D_ReleaseNotes_2023_2_1_Release_Notes_2023_2_1_known_issues_html)
rows.answer: Users complain that cloud worksharing (ACC, Revit central models, Desktop Connector) can overwrite or drop local edits during sync conflicts or failed uploads, sometimes losing hours of work. Lack of clear conflict resolution and silent failures are the core grievances.
rows.note: Sync conflicts and failed uploads dropping local edits match the Desktop Connector conflict behaviour. No source given.

rows.instruction: What do users complain about regarding Open-source commercialisation is fragile in CAD products in general?

Sustainability depends on a few maintainers and donations.

(Source: https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/29154)
rows.answer: Users note that FreeCAD 1.0 (released November 2024) integrated the topological naming mitigation from realthunder's branch, which greatly reduces broken references when earlier features are edited but does not eliminate them. Models still break in some edit cases, so careful sketch/datum practice is still advised.
rows.note: Mitigated-not-solved gist; misses issue #29154 breakage, V2 algorithm pending, open issue counts. Different source.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle XATTACH / -XREF attach, overlay, reload, unload, detach, path, type?
rows.expected: Status full: All options implemented with JSON and command-line forms; attach failure changes nothing (Evidence: crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks/xref.rs specs(); tests/xref.rs reload_unload_path_and_detach)
rows.answer: Fully: every option (attach, overlay, reload, unload, detach, path, type) is implemented with both JSON and command-line forms, and a failed attach changes nothing in the drawing. Caveats from the same card: the Unloaded state is not persisted (every xref reloads on reopen) and there is no Full/Relative/None path-type switch.
rows.note: Full, all options JSON+cmdline, failed attach changes nothing; caveats verified in referencing card.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle Nested, circular and oversized references?
rows.expected: Status full: Depth <= 16, cycle chain by canonical path, overlays not nested, file/byte/object caps (Evidence: load.rs fetch(); test circular_and_deeply_nested_references_are_bounded)
rows.answer: Nesting is bounded at depth 16, circular references are caught by a cycle chain on canonical paths, overlays are not nested, and loads are capped at 4,000,000 objects, 1,000 files, 512 MiB per file and 1 GiB total. Any such failure leaves an empty block with a status and the host drawing still opens.
rows.note: Depth 16, canonical cycle chain, overlays not nested; caps verified in load.rs constants.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle Fields, hyperlinks, dbConnect/OLE, DesignCenter, Excel links?

rows.note: None; no command specs; DATALINK CSV/TSV 8 MiB detail confirmed by card.

rows.instruction: How does CADCraft handle CSV exports (TABLEEXPORT, DATAEXTRACTION)?

rows.note: Full one-way exports in cells.rs and extract.rs, matching expected.
